newsitem.title: BELARUS: Second Russian TV crew still detained in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Second Russian TV crew still detained in Belarus.

text.p: A Russian television crew detained in Belarus remained in police custody on Sunday while their documents were being checked, a spokesman for their employers, channel ORT, said.
Their detention in a border area on Friday created new friction between Moscow and Minsk.

Dmitry Novozhilov of ORT's office in the Belarussian capital told Reuters the four-member crew was being held in the town of Lida near the Lithuanian border and could be kept in detention for up to 30 days under Belarus law.

"The conditions of their detention were more lenient when they were first arrested on Friday. They were allowed to stay overnight at a hotel and were fed at a restaurant but then had to go back to the police cells on Saturday," he said.

The Belarus border guards issued a statement on Saturday saying the four had been arrested for being in a border zone without the correct documents. It said they had been handed over to interior ministry forces while their identity was established.

On Friday, Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, who has been criticised in the West for his authoritarian style of rule, slammed Russia for checking up on his border guards' work and defended the arrest of the television crew, the second this summer.
A three-man ORT crew was detained on July 26 for violating the Belarus border. Two of the crew could face five years in prison. The third, a driver, has been released pending trial.

The second crew had intended to show that the Belarussian-Lithuanian border was not clearly defined and that the original arrests of correspondent Pavel Sheremet and his colleagues were politically inspired.
Lukashenko has constantly accused Russian media of portraying his leadership in a deliberately negative light.
He accused the ORT journalists of being in the pay of unnamed foreign powers and said he had no right to free them.

"Three are imprisoned, one is freed, and now another four went in. What can you say? What are you doing, creeping up to the border? What are four people doing there all at once?" he was quoted by Interfax-West news agency as saying on Friday.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin has said he might review a union treaty signed this year on integration between the two countries if Belarus failed to release the ORT journalists.
